column1: # Operator-attested upstream/fork commit pairs for the terraphim gitea fork.
# Format: <upstream-sha> <fork-sha>   # evidence
# Read by upstream-pick-detect.sh via --verified-picks. An entry asserts that a
# human compared the two commits and confirmed the upstream change is present in
# the fork. Use it ONLY where no machine-checkable evidence exists: the fork
# commit carries no `cherry picked from commit` or `Adapted-from:` trailer and
# its patch-id differs because the pick was adapted to fork-local code.
# This is the weakest mechanism in the detector -- it is a recorded human
# judgement, not a check. Both SHAs are re-resolved at run time and the fork
# commit must still be reachable from the searched branch, so a typo or a
# rewritten history drops the entry rather than suppressing a real gap. But if
# an adaptation were later reverted, the entry would keep suppressing. Prefer
# adding an `Adapted-from:` trailer to new picks over adding a line here.
# Both entries below predate the trailer convention. Evidence is recorded in
# .docs/research-43.md rows 6 and 9 in the terraphim/gitea repository, each
# cross-checked against the pull request that landed the pick.
# "Fix basic auth bug (#37486)". Same two files as upstream
# (services/auth/basic.go, tests/integration/oauth_test.go); patch-id differs by
# a single line in the integration test. Landed by terraphim/gitea PR #27.
# "Fix URL related escaping for oauth2 (#37334)". Adapted to the fork's OAuth
# template layout (upstream external_auth_methods.tmpl vs the fork's
# oauth_container.tmpl); remaining 13 files match upstream. Landed by
# terraphim/gitea PR #31.
